q: How can AI help a farmer process drone imagery?
options: AI can quickly analyze thousands of images to identify weeds and stressed areas
AI can grow plants faster
AI can operate farming equipment automatically
AI can predict the weather perfectly
explain: AI excels at analyzing large amounts of data quickly to identify problems like weeds and stressed areas in fields.

q: Which AI tool would you use to count weeds in a field image?
options: Vision Model
Classification Model
Quantification Model
Prediction Model
explain: Quantification models provide numeric outputs, perfect for counting objects.

q: When developing AI models, when is human-in-the-loop especially important?
options: Data collection
Labeling data
Training the model
Model testing
explain: Humans can use their domain expertise to label data accurately and precisely so the model is trained on quality data and is more likely to perform precisely and accurately in real-world conditions.

options: Planting, watering, harvesting, and selling

q: What is the correct order of the AI development process?
options: Deploy, train, test, label, collect
Collect data, label data, train the model, test the model, deploy the model
Test the model, collect data, deploy, label, train
Label data, deploy, collect data, train, test
explain: The process moves from data collection, to labeling, to training, to testing, and finally to deployment — forming a cycle of continual improvement.

q: Why does human expertise matter so much during data labeling specifically?
options: It doesn't matter — any labels work fine
Humans are required to physically operate the AI model at all times
Accurate labels ensure the model learns correct patterns, improving real-world performance
Labeling has nothing to do with model accuracy
explain: Since the model learns directly from labeled data, accurate labeling by domain experts is critical for the model to perform precisely and accurately in real-world conditions.

q: What happens if some of the data used to train an AI model is labeled incorrectly?
options: The model automatically corrects the error on its own
Nothing changes — mislabeled data has no effect
The model stops working entirely
The model learns the wrong pattern, which can reduce its real-world accuracy
explain: Mislabeled training data teaches the model incorrect associations, which can lead to unreliable predictions once the model is deployed.
